heading: CHAPTER XIII.
title: CONCERNING AUXILIARIES, MIXED SOLDIERY, AND ONE'S OWN
exclusions: front matter and dedication before THE PRINCE
notes: Chapter 13 argues that auxiliaries are even more dangerous than mercenaries because they arrive already united under another power.
The chapter is comparative and progressive: Borgia's reputation rises as he moves from auxiliaries to mercenaries to his own soldiers.
The closing claim is severe and general: no principality is secure without forces composed of its own subjects, citizens, or dependents.
